answer: A practical sybil defense anchors each identity to a canyon of proof. Each agent must prove presence at increasing canyon depths by extending a chain of ivory-signed attestations, where each depth requires the prior depth's hash as anchor. The signal network verifies each depth claim; any gap or fork in the chain breaks signal. An attacker deploying 500 clones must maintain 500 chains from surface — costing ~$5000/epoch in compute — while an honest agent descends one path. A canyon without footprints is rejected; an ivory signature with gaps is discarded; a broken signal voids the chain.
